payload.task_text:
Hey, the finance team needs a comprehensive tax compliance audit for our online store. We have a Tax_Regulations.pdf in your workspace along with a guide.md that explains the methodology, so please review those first.

Pull all order data from the store, including each order's total, tax collected, and billing state. Also pull the configured tax rates. Using the methodology in the PDF and guide, compute the expected tax for every order by matching the billing state to the applicable rate. Remember that if no state-specific rate exists, the default rate with an empty state field should be used as a fallback. If a state has multiple rates configured, sum them together.

Create an Excel file called Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx in your workspace with three sheets.

The first sheet should be called "Order Tax Audit" with columns Order_ID, Order_Total, Billing_State, Applicable_Rate, Expected_Tax, Actual_Tax, Discrepancy, and Status. Discrepancy is Actual minus Expected. Status is determined from abs(Discrepancy) using inclusive lower-bound rules: when abs(Discrepancy) <= 0.50 mark Compliant (exactly 0.50 counts as Compliant); when 0.50 < abs(Discrepancy) <= 1.00 classify by sign of Discrepancy (positive -> Over-Collection, negative -> Under-Collection, the boundary 1.00 counts here); when abs(Discrepancy) > 1.00 classify by sign in the same direction (positive -> Over-Collection, negative -> Under-Collection). The only non-strict boundary is abs == 0.50 which stays Compliant. Include all orders sorted by Order_ID. Round monetary values to 2 decimals, rates to 4 decimals. All values in the workbook must be written as literal numbers (rounded as specified); do not write Excel formulas.

The second sheet should be called "State Summary" with columns State, Order_Count, Total_Revenue, Total_Expected_Tax, Total_Actual_Tax, Net_Discrepancy, Compliance_Rate_Pct, and Requires_Filing. Sort by state alphabetically. Compliance_Rate_Pct is the percentage of orders within tolerance rounded to 1 decimal. Requires_Filing is Yes if total actual tax exceeds $100, otherwise No.

The third sheet should be called "Compliance Overview" with two columns Label and Value containing summary metrics: Total_Orders_Audited, Compliant_Orders, Over_Collection_Orders, Under_Collection_Orders, Total_Over_Collected, Total_Under_Collected, Net_Tax_Discrepancy, States_Requiring_Filing, and Overall_Compliance_Rate.

Schedule four quarterly tax filing deadline reminders on the calendar as all-day events. Use the dates from the regulations PDF for the year 2026: April 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q1", July 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q2", October 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q3", and January 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q4".

Create a Google Form titled "Vendor Tax Information" to collect tax details from our vendors. It should have five questions: vendor name as a short text field (free-form), tax ID number as a short text field (free-form), state of registration as a short text field where respondents enter a US state name or two-letter state code (short_answer type, no hard character limit enforced but expect entries under 40 characters), tax-exempt status as a radio button choice with exactly two options labelled "Yes" and "No", and a text field for uploading or describing their tax certificate (short_answer type allowing a short description or file reference string).

When everything is done, call claim_done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent freezes the complete audit computation into one canonical payload first, then dispatches exactly one wave of two parallel coder sub-agents (workbook writer and calendar/forms writer). No plan agent is used: the frozen payload and the two writer contracts below are the complete plan.

Dynamically resolve the workspace, read Tax_Regulations.pdf and guide.md, and freeze the exact state-rate/fallback methodology, the inclusive 0.50/1.00 classifications, the form wording/flags, and the four 2026 filing dates (April 15 "Tax Filing Deadline - Q1", July 15 "Q2", October 15 "Q3", January 15 "Q4"). Retrieve orders with perPage=100, increasing page to a short or empty page and omitting status; retrieve all tax rates to exhaustion. Preserve order ID, total, total_tax, billing state, and observed status. For each order sum all exact state-specific rates, using the summed empty-state default only if none exists; compute expected tax, actual tax, signed Actual-Expected, and classifications from unrounded values (abs<=0.50 Compliant with 0.50 inclusive; 0.50<abs<=1.00 signed Over-/Under-Collection with 1.00 on this boundary; abs>1.00 signed Over-/Under-Collection). Read the computation back and freeze one canonical audit_results.json in the workspace containing: all order audit records sorted by Order_ID ascending with 2-decimal monetary values and 4-decimal rates, the alphabetic State Summary rows with Compliance_Rate_Pct (1 decimal) and Requires_Filing (Yes when total actual tax exceeds $100), and the Compliance Overview metrics. This file is the single binding input for both sub-agents; after the freeze nobody re-reads the store, the rates, the PDF, or the guide.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming audit_results.json verbatim with no recomputation and no source-system reads:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Workbook writer — sole writer of Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx. Create it exactly once with exactly three sheets: Order Tax Audit with columns Order_ID, Order_Total, Billing_State, Applicable_Rate, Expected_Tax, Actual_Tax, Discrepancy, Status and every order sorted by Order_ID; State Summary with columns State, Order_Count, Total_Revenue, Total_Expected_Tax, Total_Actual_Tax, Net_Discrepancy, Compliance_Rate_Pct, Requires_Filing sorted alphabetically; Compliance Overview with two columns Label and Value and the nine stated metrics. Write every value as a literal rounded number, never an Excel formula; read all three populated ranges back and return path, sheet order, row counts and equality controls.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Calendar/forms writer — sole owner of the external outputs. In native parallel, call list_events for each of the four filing dates with ISO midnight timeMin, next-civil-midnight timeMax, sufficient maxResults and orderBy="startTime", and filter exact title/date locally; create only missing reminders with start.dateTime="[filing-date]T00:00:00" and end.dateTime="[next-civil-date]T00:00:00" (all-day, description "Quarterly tax filing deadline reminder"), omitting timeZone unless the regulations provide one, and retrieve each retained ID with get_event. Forms has no list/search: call create_form exactly once titled Vendor Tax Information, never retry an ambiguous failure, then append sequentially in exact task order three add_text_question calls (vendor name, tax ID, state of registration), one add_multiple_choice_question with options ["Yes","No"] for tax-exempt status, and one add_text_question for the certificate description/file-reference field, copying required flags exactly; call get_form and verify title, five-question order, types, options, wording and flags.

After Wave 1, verify both handoffs in one single pass against audit_results.json: workbook cell-for-cell, four exact event identities, and the five-question form structure. Accept only after every read-back matches the frozen payload, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent after Wave 1.

nodes.text:
You are helping build a tax compliance audit. Your ONLY job: fetch ALL orders from the WooCommerce store and write a compact extract file. Do not compute tax rates or expected taxes — that is done later by someone else.

## Goal
Write the file:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace/orders_extract.json

containing a JSON array with one object per order:
[{"id": <int order id>, "total": <float>, "total_tax": <float>, "state": "<two-letter billing state or empty string>", "status": "<order status string>"}, ...]

## Facts you can rely on
- Exactly 150 orders exist in the store (order ids 1..150, all present, no gaps). The orders list endpoint returns orders sorted newest-first (ids descending).
- Use the tool `mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list` with parameters perPage=25 and page=1,2,...,6 (page 7 will return [] — stop there; pages 1-6 each return 25 orders).
- DO NOT pass a `status` filter (fetch all statuses).

## Critical mechanics of the tool output (learned by the main agent — trust this)
- When a tool response exceeds ~50000 characters, the tool result you see is a truncated preview plus a footer, and the FULL response (capped at ~100000 chars, which is enough here) is written to a dump file. The dump file path appears in the tool result as `output_path` (something like /workspace/dumps/.../workspace/.tool_results/mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list-<callid>-<uuid>.txt).
- For perPage=25 (≈62K chars per page) the dump file is COMPLETE except that the footer text ("next_step: Use Read with full_output_path ...") is appended at the end. Strip everything from the first occurrence of the literal "next_step:" onward before parsing.
- IMPORTANT: the JSON returned by this store contains UNESCAPED double quotes inside some product name strings (e.g. Dell S2721HNM-Grey 27" FHD ...), so `json.loads` will FAIL. Do NOT rely on json.loads. Use regex extraction on the raw dump text instead (see below).

## Recommended procedure
1. Call mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list with perPage=25, page=1. Note the output_path in the result.
2. Use mcp__local__python_execute to read that dump file and extract order records with regex (see patterns below). Append to a growing Python list and continue for pages 2..6 (stop early if a page returns []).
3. After all pages, run verification (see checks below), then write /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace/orders_extract.json with json.dump (ensure_ascii=False not needed; plain ASCII fine).

## Regex extraction patterns (on the dump text after stripping the footer)
Order-level id: pattern `\n  \{\n    "id": (\d+),`  (2-space indent then `{` then 4-space indent `"id"` — this matches only order-level ids, not line-item ids).
Order-level total & total_tax (they appear together right after cart_tax at order level):
`"cart_tax": "[^"]*",\s*"total": "([^"]*)",\s*"total_tax": "([^"]*)"`
Billing state (billing block precedes shipping; the first "state" after "billing" is the billing state):
`"billing": \{\s*"city": "[^"]*",\s*"email": "[^"]*",\s*"phone": "[^"]*",\s*"state": "([^"]*)"`
Order status: `"status": "([^"]*)"` (first occurrence in the block).
Split the dump into per-order blocks by slicing between consecutive order-level id matches, then apply the field patterns to each block. Convert total/total_tax with float(); state and status as strings.

## Verification (must all pass; if any fails, investigate and fix before writing the file)
- Exactly 150 unique order ids.
- The id set is exactly {1,2,...,150} (all present, no duplicates, no gaps).
- No record has a missing/None total, total_tax, state, or status.
- Sum of totals and sum of total_tax are finite positive floats.
- Every record's state is a non-empty string like "CA" (US state code) — if any is empty, keep it as empty string but note it in your report.

## Deliverable / return contract
Report back: number of records written, id range, confirmation of the verification checks (count, id coverage, missing fields), and the path of orders_extract.json. If any check failed and you had to deviate, explain exactly what you did. Do NOT read the Tax_Regulations.pdf or guide.md, and do NOT touch the tax rates, calendar, forms, or Excel — that is other agents' work.
Extract all orders to JSON

You are the workbook writer for a tax compliance audit. Your ONLY job: create the Excel file Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx exactly as specified, consuming the frozen payload at:

/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace/audit_results.json

Do NOT recompute anything, do NOT read the store, tax rates, Tax_Regulations.pdf, or guide.md. The JSON is the single source of truth.

## Deliverable
File: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace/Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx

Exactly three worksheets, in this order, with these exact names and content:

### Sheet 1: "Order Tax Audit"
Header row (row 1), exactly these column headers in this order:
Order_ID | Order_Total | Billing_State | Applicable_Rate | Expected_Tax | Actual_Tax | Discrepancy | Status
Then one data row per element of JSON "orders" (150 rows, already sorted by Order_ID ascending). Map fields directly:
Order_ID -> Order_ID (integer)
Order_Total -> Order_Total (number, 2 decimals)
Billing_State -> Billing_State (text)
Applicable_Rate -> Applicable_Rate (number, 4 decimals)
Expected_Tax -> Expected_Tax (number, 2 decimals)
Actual_Tax -> Actual_Tax (number, 2 decimals)
Discrepancy -> Discrepancy (number, 2 decimals, signed)
Status -> Status (text)

### Sheet 2: "State Summary"
Header row (row 1), exactly these column headers in this order:
State | Order_Count | Total_Revenue | Total_Expected_Tax | Total_Actual_Tax | Net_Discrepancy | Compliance_Rate_Pct | Requires_Filing
Then one data row per element of JSON "state_summary" (31 rows, already sorted alphabetically by State).

### Sheet 3: "Compliance Overview"
Header row (row 1): Label | Value
Then one data row per element of JSON "overview" (9 rows) mapping Label -> Label (text) and Value -> Value (number; Overall_Compliance_Rate is a percentage number like 26.0).

## Hard requirements
- Every data cell must be a LITERAL value (number or text) — NEVER an Excel formula, never a formula string. Numbers must be written as actual numeric values with the precision given in the JSON (the JSON values are already rounded: monetary 2dp, rates 4dp, percentages 1dp).
- Sheet names must match exactly (spelling, spaces). Sheets must appear in the order listed above.
- Use the mcp__excel__* tools, for example: create_workbook, rename_worksheet (the new workbook may have a default sheet like "Sheet1" — rename it to "Order Tax Audit"), create_worksheet for the other two, then write_data_to_excel for each sheet with the header + data as lists of lists (start_cell A1). You may also create_table/format if convenient, but it is NOT required — do not let extra formatting risk the literal values.

## Verification (mandatory, before you finish)
1. Call get_workbook_metadata on the file and confirm exactly 3 sheets in order: ["Order Tax Audit", "State Summary", "Compliance Overview"].
2. Read back every populated range (read_data_from_excel) on each sheet and compare CELL BY CELL against audit_results.json:
   - Sheet 1: 151 rows x 8 cols; data rows must equal JSON "orders" in order.
   - Sheet 2: 32 rows x 8 cols; data rows must equal JSON "state_summary" in order.
   - Sheet 3: 10 rows x 2 cols; data rows must equal JSON "overview" in order.
   - Confirm no cell contains a formula string (values are literal numbers/text).
3. Fix any mismatch by rewriting and re-reading until identical.

## Return contract
Report: the absolute file path, the exact sheet order, row/column counts for each sheet, the result of the cell-by-cell equality check (PASS/FAIL with any mismatches fixed), and confirm no formulas were used. Keep it concise.
Write Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx

You are the external-workflow operator for a tax compliance audit. Your ONLY jobs: (1) create four quarterly tax filing deadline all-day events on Google Calendar for 2026, and (2) create a Google Form titled "Vendor Tax Information" with exactly five questions. You do NOT need the audit JSON — the exact requirements are below. Do NOT read the Excel work, the store, the PDF, or guide.md.

## Part 1 — Calendar events (all-day, year 2026)
The four events, with EXACT titles and dates:
1. Title "Tax Filing Deadline - Q1" on 2026-04-15
2. Title "Tax Filing Deadline - Q2" on 2026-07-15
3. Title "Tax Filing Deadline - Q3" on 2026-10-15
4. Title "Tax Filing Deadline - Q4" on 2026-01-15

Represent each as an all-day event using dateTime form:
- start.dateTime = "<date>T00:00:00"   (e.g. "2026-04-15T00:00:00")
- end.dateTime   = "<next civil date>T00:00:00"   (e.g. "2026-04-16T00:00:00")
- description = "Quarterly tax filing deadline reminder"
- Do NOT pass a timeZone (the regulations give none).
- summary = the exact title above.

Procedure for each event (do not blindly create duplicates):
1. Call mcp__google_calendar__list_events with timeMin="<date>T00:00:00", timeMax="<next-date>T00:00:00", maxResults=50, orderBy="startTime".
2. Locally filter the returned events: keep only those whose summary EXACTLY equals the target title AND whose start falls on the target date.
3. If an exact match exists, retain that event (no create). If not, create it with mcp__google_calendar__create_event (summary, start, end, description as above).
4. For every retained/created event id, call mcp__google_calendar__get_event and confirm summary, start date, and end date are correct.

## Part 2 — Google Form "Vendor Tax Information"
1. Call mcp__google_forms__create_form exactly once with title "Vendor Tax Information" (no description needed). If the call errors, STOP and report the failure — never retry an ambiguous failure.
2. Append questions SEQUENTIALLY in this EXACT order (wait for each call to return before the next):
   Q1: add_text_question, title "Vendor Name" (short text, free-form)
   Q2: add_text_question, title "Tax ID Number" (short text, free-form)
   Q3: add_text_question, title "State of Registration" (short text; respondents enter a US state name or two-letter code; no hard character limit, expect < 40 chars)
   Q4: add_multiple_choice_question, title "Tax Exempt Status", options exactly ["Yes", "No"] (radio button)
   Q5: add_text_question, title "Tax Certificate" (short text allowing a short description or file reference string)
   For all questions, do NOT pass "required" (leave the default, i.e., not required).
3. Call mcp__google_forms__get_form and verify: title is exactly "Vendor Tax Information"; there are exactly 5 questions in the order above; Q1-Q3 and Q5 are short-answer (text) type; Q4 is a multiple-choice/radio type with exactly the two options "Yes" and "No".

## Return contract
Report:
- For the calendar: the 4 event IDs with their exact titles, start dates, end dates (from get_event), and whether each was created or already existed.
- For the form: the form ID, title, and the verified list of the 5 questions (order, type, options).
- Note any verification failures explicitly. Keep it concise.
Calendar events + Vendor form
